title: cw: a high-level repository tour
summary: Follow a walkthrough from its JSON contract through validation, web delivery and VS Code navigation, then see how local questions and authoring instructions fit around it. This is an architectural orientation; deployment, authentication internals and worktree management are outside the route. Inspected working tree: 2026-09-11, based on c7c69d9677e9, including local VS Code additions. Commit links are recorded only for files identical to that revision.

parts.title: One document, a shared contract
parts.summary: The document contains the explanation; schema and semantic checks make it portable.

sections.title: One document, a shared contract
sections.summary: The document contains the explanation; schema and semantic checks make it portable.

blocks.text: The main unit is a JSON document containing parts, sections and steps. Each cw/2 step holds an ordered list of blocks: prose, code, callouts, diagrams, diffs, timelines or an extension fallback. A new topic needs a document, not a new screen implementation.

flowchart TB
  A[Author or skill] --> D[cw/2 JSON]
  D --> V[Schema checks]
  V --> L[Local web]
  V --> H[Hosted web]
  V --> E[VS Code]
  L --> C[Local comments]
  E --> C
blocks.alt: An author writes cw/2 JSON. Validation checks the contract. Local web, hosted web and VS Code read it; the local readers also connect to local comments.
blocks.caption: The contract is shared. Go and the VS Code extension implement their own validation and rendering. Click a reader or the comments node to visit its code.

snippet.label: The top-level document
snippet.text:
type Doc2 struct {
	Schema   string                     `json:"$schema,omitempty"`
	Version  string                     `json:"version"`
	Title    string                     `json:"title"`
	Summary  string                     `json:"summary,omitempty"`
	Language string                     `json:"language,omitempty"`
	Source   *Source2                   `json:"source,omitempty"`
	Parts    []Part2                    `json:"parts"`
	Ext      map[string]json.RawMessage `json:"ext,omitempty"`
}

snippet.label: Steps carry ordered blocks
snippet.text:
type Step2 struct {
	ID     string                     `json:"id"`
	Title  string                     `json:"title"`
	Speech string                     `json:"speech,omitempty"`
	Blocks []Block                    `json:"blocks"`
	Ext    map[string]json.RawMessage `json:"ext,omitempty"`
}

blocks.text: ParseDoc in load.go is the Go entry point for document bytes. It chooses the schema from version, validates the shape, and then runs inspect2 for cw/2 rules such as snippet ranges and diagram references. The schema lives in schema/; spec/FORMAT.md explains its meaning. Unsupported versions are refused.

snippet.label: Version selects the contract
Then check cw/2 meaning

blocks.text: The Go application also retains cw/1 support for older documents. The VS Code extension intentionally accepts cw/2 only.

parts.title: Read the same content in different places
parts.summary: The local server supplies machine access, the site distributes documents, and VS Code opens source directly.

sections.title: Read the same content in different places
sections.summary: The local server supplies machine access, the site distributes documents, and VS Code opens source directly.

steps.title: The local server joins document and checkout

blocks.text: cw serve loads the file and resolves the repository root. It creates a local server with the document, checkout and comment store. That root is a fact about this reading session; cw/2 does not embed a machine-specific checkout path. main.go wires the service; doc.go handles local snippet verification.

snippet.label: A document plus local context

steps.title: The browser renders blocks in order

blocks.text: web/app.js owns the overview, navigation and reader shell; web/state.js owns reading state. The selected version renderer builds each step. For cw/2, web/render2.js walks the authored blocks in order, keeping explanation and evidence together. web/ui.js supplies shared rendering and editor-link helpers.

snippet.label: The cw/2 rendering loop

steps.title: Publishing separates content from a local machine

blocks.text: The hosted API retrieves a stored document and packages it for the browser. Its payload contains the JSON, publication metadata and source links. store.go persists hosted data; gate.go controls read access. The hosted page links to repository code; checkout verification and local questions belong to the local readers.

snippet.label: The hosted reader payload

steps.title: VS Code keeps explanation beside real code

blocks.text: vscode-extension/ is a separate TypeScript reader. model.ts validates the shared cw/2 schema and resolves copied snippets; render.ts and sidebar.ts build the explanation. extension.ts opens the matching file, decorates it and selects the relevant line. remote.ts downloads published documents. This excerpt starts after snippet resolution has established a usable range.

snippet.label: Open and reveal the verified source location

parts.summary: Local questions do not change the walkthrough; shared instructions help authors create it.

steps.title: Questions belong to a reading session

blocks.text: comments.go owns local threads and the cw comments watch/reply workflow. Comment files live beside user settings, not beside the walkthrough. The local server is their only writer. The web reader uses that service directly; VS Code connects through vscode-extension/src/comments.ts and can start its bundled cw helper.

snippet.label: Comments have their own storage location

steps.title: The same guidance reaches local authors and the site

blocks.text: skills/code-walkthrough/ explains scope, evidence and cw/2 fields. docs.go embeds the shared rules and field reference and assembles them with the API instructions for /skill.md. Authoring guidance stays close to the format rather than inside a reader. examples/ provides documents to try, including this one.

snippet.label: Assemble the agent-facing instructions

blocks.title: Where to start a change
blocks.text: For document meaning, start in schema/ and spec/. For browser behavior, start in web/. For native editor behavior, start in vscode-extension/src/. For local feedback, start in comments.go. Validate an edited walkthrough with cw check before trying it in a reader.
